text:
Maya Chen: Heads up — CUST-42 legal sent a draft that ties private deployment to a 99.95% uptime SLA and specific RPO for control plane. Need quick alignment on scope we can commit to before sales pushes deadline tomorrow.
Jason Li: 99.95% for control plane in private (VPC) is possible with dedicated control-plane replicas + cross-region failover, but for on-prem boxed installs it's trickier. Need clear matrix.
Samir Khatri: Agree. On-prem boxed = we can do single-region HA if customer provides two datacenters. Air-gapped customers add packaging work: offline installer, signed manifests, and manual upgrade playbook.
Priya Nair: Legal flag — contract language currently says "Redwood shall ensure control plane availability" with penalty clauses. We should avoid open-ended commitments for on-prem. Propose tiered SLA.
Leila Ortiz: From sales: CUST-42 will pay for enterprise tier if we give them 99.95 for VPC/private-hosted. They expect on-prem parity but may accept delayed GA for airgap if we offer migration credits.
Jason Li: Proposal: Offer two SKUs in contract: VPC-ControlPlane (99.95 SLA) and OnPrem-ControlPlane (90-day GA with best-effort, then SLA after onboarding). That buys engineering time for packaging.
Maya Chen: That maps to product roadmap choices. We need to decide which workstreams to prioritize this quarter: (A) Harden VPC control-plane HA + runbooks, (B) On-prem installer + airgap packaging, (C) Legal/contract templating and SLO observability. Thoughts?
Samir Khatri: Implementation effort estimate: A = 3 sprints (replication + failover tests + monitoring), B = 4-5 sprints (packaging, offline deps, signed artifacts), C = 1 sprint (SLO metrics + contract boilerplate).
Priya Nair: Legal prefers explicit clauses: what counts as downtime, maintenance windows, and customer responsibilities for on-prem hardware. I'll draft language if we agree on tiering.
Leila Ortiz: Customers with procurement cycles want defined SLAs. If we present phased GA (VPC first, then on-prem), we should provide timeline and rollback options.
Maya Chen: Risk table quick take — A low risk, high impact for revenue; B medium risk, high engineering cost; C low cost, necessary for contract signoff. Recommend prioritize A + C this quarter, B as Q+1 with pilot.
Jason Li: +1 for A+C. For B, we can parallelize packaging owners: eng-packaging + release. I'll assign small spike to estimate airgap edge cases (HSM, offline license activation).
Samir Khatri: Spike noted. Also need to confirm KMS/HSM support matrix for on-prem customers — call with infra partner required.
Maya Chen: Action items: Priya to draft SLA tier language by EOD, Jason to post spike plan and owners, Samir to coord infra partner, Leila to communicate phased approach to CUST-42. I'll summarize and get exec signoff.
Priya Nair: Will draft. Quick Q: Do we want automatic fallback in contract to hosted Redwood if on-prem control plane becomes unhealthy?
Leila Ortiz: Customers won't like automatic failover to our hosted plane without explicit consent — propose opt-in fallback as an add-on.
Jason Li: Technically doable but requires networking consent and data residency opt-in. Flagging compliance review.
LegalBot: Reminder: add maintenance window exceptions and force majeure clause. Also define "control plane unavailability" as failure of API endpoints across all healthy replicas for more than X minutes.
Maya Chen: Good point — define X = 30 min for tiered SLA, but we can make X configurable per customer at higher price.
deploy-bot: CI/CD note — automating signed offline bundles requires build infra changes; estimate 2 infra tickets.
Maya Chen: OK team — I'll lock A+C in this quarter's roadmap. We'll add B as a phased epic with pilot targets and acceptance criteria. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Jason Li: Thanks — will share spike plan in #eng-runtime by EOD.
Leila Ortiz: I'll draft the customer-facing timeline and send to Maya for review.
Priya Nair: Draft SLA language uploaded to Google Drive (link internal). I'll ping once ready.
Maya Chen: Closing thread — we'll review in tomorrow's roadmap sync at 10:00. If anyone has blocking concerns, DM me.
